commits.message:
parser: avoid deleting files for unified diffs that only empty them

A unified diff that removes all lines from a file uses a new file range of
0,0, but that does not mean the file should be deleted. We were inferring
Operation::Delete from that hunk header alone, so applying such a patch
removed the target file entirely instead of leaving it as an empty file.

Match traditional patch behavior by only inferring add/delete from /dev/null
headers when file paths are present, and keep the old hunk-range fallback for
headerless cases.

file: handle EOF explicitly in File::peek

fgetc() returns an int so it can represent every byte value plus EOF.
Casting that result directly to char loses the EOF sentinel and can
produce an ordinary byte value instead, depending on the platform's
char signedness.
applier: fix pluralization for negative hunk offsets
applier: handle empty input correctly when closing --ifdef hunks
meta: remove sonar github action
meta: bump MSVC upload artifact version
tests: improve assertion output to better show whitespace differences

system: remove unused filesystem::file_size(const std::string&)

This is no longer needed now that we are using the C FILE* overload of
this function.

patch: do not issue spurious warning removing a file in dry-run

Since dry run was not writing to the output file, the file size was
being determined as non-empty. To fix this, simply check for this on the
temporary file which has been written to, even on a dry run.

file: implement the ability to determine a files size

From a c FILE*.
patch: also write reject file when outputting to stdout

patch: use `inform_hunks_failed` in another applicable case

Turns out there already 3 cases of this, not just 2!
patch: factor out a function to write out the patched file
patch: put ed unsupported exception into diff_format_from_options
meta: disable some annoying clang-tidy warnings
patch: factor out read-only permission fixup into a function

patch: factor out a common inform_hunks_failed function

We already had two places which implemented this logic, and I am
thinking of adding a third. Factor out a function to show this user
input.

formatter: do not output timestamps for /dev/null files

GNU patch does not seem to output timestamps for /dev/null even though
the diff utility appears to. To preserve compatability with reject
files, avoid outputing a timestamp for this case.

applier: factor out a function to prompt user for reverse handling

This function is useful in other contexts as well.
applier: ensure reversing patch also reverses operation

options: update copyright in help message

It's 2024 now :^)

locator: correctly reject patches adding a file for non-empty files

This corrects the actual logic needed to fix the:
`applier_add_file_but_file_already_exits_with_conflicts` test.

We just need to also add an informational message about when this case
is detected.

applier: correct logic for printing location of failed hunk

We were not correctly considering the case that the old file was empty.
To fix this, use the same logic as what is used in the locator to
determine the expected file location when printing this information.

tests: add a test for a failure applying patch adding file

It seems that for this case we are assuming that everything is fine, and
will apply the patch even though:

 1. The file already exists! (GNU patch seems to warn for this case)
 2. Even after confirming that we do not mind that the file already
    exists, we do not detect that there the content in that file
    _should_ cause that patch to fail.
patch: remove unused system include from file.h header
patch: Fix mistakenly hardcoded prerequisite string

patch: simplify handling of adding a file

Instead of using a separately managed variable, just fully rely on what
the patch header is telling us.
formatted: removed unused line_num variable

parser: rename to_lines_expected to new_lines_expected

For nice symmetry with old_lines_expected.
options: only perform a single write when writing version message

cmdline: factor out a cmdline handler to make option parsing generic

The cmdline parser can now be used for parsing commandlines other than
just what we expect for patch. This is done by factoring out a class
that has a virtual process_option function. Inheriting command line
handlers can implement this to interpret the given option in the
application specific method.

meta: add some more information to the readme

There is a lot that could be added here, and there is probably a much
better way of writing it - but we have to start somewhere!

parser: move parse_git_extended_info into line parser

Making the function read a whole lot nicer!

parser: use reference instead of pointer in parse_normal_patch

At some stage this was factored to never be non null, so use a reference
here instead to show that.

parser: simplify check for end of patch in parse_unified_patch

If we were at the last line we can immediately stop parsing the patch.

parser: factor some functions to make use of line parser

In particular, this has the nice side effect of slightly simplifying
parse_git_header_name to not have a dead check for the git header.

We are also able to remove LineParser::end() and LineParser::current()
with these changes.

Finally, this allows us to get rid of the substr with magic number
checks when parsing file names.

parser: move definitions of line parser to header file

So that it can in the future be used by unit tests more easily.
parser: factor out need for m_line member

parser: ignore file modes that have an invalid format

Instead of our previous approach of aborting with an exception. While
making this change, also handle a few more cases of the mode string
being invalid.
tests: add a test for a bad --newline-output option
tests: add a test case coverage --reject-format=unified

tests: add tests for bad options for --read-only and --reject-format

Put in as a unit test instead of running the binary itself as the error
message for this that I get on my own system is not too informative, and
I do not want to be mimicking this behaviour.

tests: add test for --read-only=warn flag

Which we already handle by default, but didn't have a test for when the
flag is explicitly given.

meta: exclude throw branches when generating coverage

In hopes of improving the quality of the coverage report.

formatter: use character format output where relevant

This overload is (slightly) more efficient than the const char* one, so
use char where possible.

tests: add some more test cases for file implementation

Just to catch some missing coverage.

applier: remove incorrect comment

This comment was a copy paste from an older version of the code and no
longer applies to the define handling.

applier: simplify logic for determining newlines

There was some dead code for the Newline::None case. Remove this branch
in favour of a if/else statement.

patch: add initial support for adding symlinks

We still need to add Windows support, and there are a whole bunch of
cases that are not tested yet, but this does appear to correctly add
symlinks on my system for a barebones symlink patch.

patch: improve support for quoting shell style strings

This is definitely still not fully accurate and does not handle multiple
types of quotes in the same string - but at the very least this should
still serve as an improvement over the previous implementation.

patch: improve support for quoting c style strings

Surely there is more to do here, but this should serve as a good first
pass at supporting this.

parser: fix strip including backslash on non windows platforms

Which broke things if there was a backslash in the filename as it was
being considered a path separator.

patch: add initial support for quoting-style

We have a really naive implementation for quoting with this initial pass
- but that is to be improved! For now, just begin with the basic
plumbing so that the option exists.

patch: begin adding initial support for handling symlinks

git patches seem to have support for symlinks. From what I can tell,
this is signalled by the mode of the patch file.

For now, only add support for the "symbollic link" prompt which is given
when given a symlink patch. Soon, we should also handle actually adding
the symlink itself!
tests: fix failing tests incorrectly passing

cmdline: add support for POSIXLY_CORRECT environment variable

This serves as the alternative way of putting patch into POSIX mode.
tests: put patch/test.h under a Patch namespace

patch: fix normal patches not removing empty files after patch

Normal patches do not have the /dev/null file paths to be using whether
the patch is removing the file or not. Instead use the proper check for
removal which instead takes into account the hunk range in the patch
header.

patch: fix git patches not correctly removing empty files

The deferred write mechanism was resulting in the following
remove-if-empty check to incorrectly determine that there was some
mismatch in applying the removal patch, so we should not be removing the
file altogether.

This _may_ be hacky (and I am not sure if this causes other problems
yet), but to fix this, we now immediately apply git removal patches
instead of deferring it.
tests: fix xfail tests passing on an unexpected pass
tests: add a failing test for removing empty file for normal patch

tests: add ability for patch specific xfail

This is intended to be used when there is some test case that we are
failing on but other patch programs successfully pass.

patch: implement --remove-empty-files with --posix handling

Functionally the only real difference here to our existing logic is that
the removal of empty files now does not happen if the --posix option is
set.

parser: fix a case of incorrectly parsing normal diff ranges

I created a normal diff where I was trying to have the file removed.
It wasn't! The parsing of the patch was actually not working altogether!
Turns out that the root cause stemmed from the normal range not being
parsed as expected, and the parser was trying to fetch one two many
lines from the normal patch.

patch: do not back on mismatch by default if --posix flag set

If the --posix option is set we now will only backup files if explicitly
told to so.

tests: add ability for expected failure compatibility tests

These are intended to be used when a test is failing in our
compatibility test (due to a bug), but this implementation is working as
expected.

cmdline: add a --posix commandline flag

This will be used to change the defaults of some options closer to the
posix standard.

file: fix not moving all state on file move construct or assign

We were not also moving the bad and eof bits when move constructing and
move assigning a file. Add this in, and a corresponding unit test for it
as well. While we are at it, rename some of the members so that they
also have the m_ prefix.

file: factor opening of file to common helper function

Which is soley responsible for handling the platform specifics.

patch: implement options to enable/disable backups on mismatch

Add the options to enable or disable the behaviour of applying backups
on mismatch. The '--backup-if-mimatch' option is kind of useless at the
moment since it defaults to true, and the only way to turn it off is the
'--no-backup-if-mismatch' option. However, this should change as soon as
the '--posix' option is introduced which will be changing some of these
defaults!

file: improve error handling

We were not correctly checking for errors in a place we were calling
fwrite. Factor out some helpers to consolidate some error checking.
tests: add some more tests for corrupted unified ranges

parser: remove some dead code

Not sure what these checks are trying to achieve!

applier: fix --ifdef behaviour on line added and then removed

I was juts trying to add test coverage to this piece of code, and then
realised that the implementation was actually broken for this case! diff
does not seem to really produce diffs that have lines added before
removals, but support this anyway since it's still a valid patch file.
tests: improve assertion result on failure
applier: add support for --batch option for reversed patches

patch: add support for --batch and --force options for prerequisites

--batch being an entirely new option altogether which we did not
previously support! It seems from reading the man page of patch that
--batch is used for more than just this, but this should serve as a good
initial go at it.

patch: begin adding ability to handle Prereq lines in patch

There is still probably a bunch more to implement here, but this should
at least give us a basic start at it!
parser: add ability to parse prerequisite line in patch header
tests: port test_reject to patch test

tests: port test_applier unit tests to patch test

Hopefully reducing future maintaince when making internal API changes.

patch: remove some broken logic checking for empty file

We don't actually have any test case for this but the test case is
causing another test case (to be added) to fail. So until we actually
implement this with some tests, just remove the logic entirely.
tests: port test_defines to patch test

patch: fix being unable to add a file in a normal patch

Our approach of just using the filename of /dev/null to determine
whether we are adding a file or not does not work for normal patch as it
does not contain any patch header with a filename in it.

There is some code here that is starting to look pretty nasty, but I'm
not entirely sure yet of the behaviour which we intend to implement, so
that should be fine for now.

parser: further improve error messages output by corrupted normal patch

Cover off some more possibilities for corrupted normal patches, making
sure that we report a sane error if that goes wrong.

parser: remove an unnecessary eof check

This should have been checked earlier on when trying to find the patch
in the first place.

parser: detect and improve error on some more context patch cases

Further work towards improving the quality of errors which are reported
on a corrupted context patch.

parser: improve error on a corrupted context patch

If a line being parsed is expected to contain a patch content line, but
the operation for that line is not valid then error out with a parser
error. Also ensure that we throw an informative error here that also
says the line number and the content of the line which was just parsed.

The stdout output here is the same as what is done for a unified patch,
but is not the same as what GNU patch does. Therefore, for now, we don't
add a test for it. Hopefully this behavioural difference isn't as a
result of some other underlying issue.

While we are at it, move all context patch specific tests into their own
file.

parser: improve error on a corrupted normal patch

Which also requires us to increase the robustness of parsing such a
patch in the first place! We now parse normal patches with some better
understanding of how the patch is meant to be structured, instead of
simply goign through each line and blindly adding things in.
tests: add a test for now newline at eof for removal normal patch

patch: do not use std::tmpfile to create temporary files

tmpfile on windows unfortunately may need admin privileges to run. To
solve this problem write our own implementation of creating a temporary
file.

This should also allow us future optimisations where we can perhaps make
us of the filename to rename the temporary file, instead of needing to
copy the entire thing.

patch: fix various compiler warnings

Mostly ones complaining about sign conversion.

applier: fold some logic into a common boolean variable

To improve readability.
tests: add a test for applying a patch that has already been applied

applier: remove uneeded error check when reading lines of file

The `get_line` function already error checks this for us, and will
throw an exception if needed.

parser: slightly simplify some logic in parse_normal_range

And add some more tests while we are at it.

applier: consider hunk reversed if forwards applies but reversed doesn't

Fixing scenarios where the patch has been accidentally reversed and the
patch reversed will not apply without any fuzz.
parser: slightly simplify some logic in parse_unified_patch

tests: improve test coverage on matches_ignoring_whitespace

Cover off some paths which were not covered off previously.

parser: improve usefulness of error thrown on corrupted patch

Also include the line number and the contents of the line which is
corrupted.
